why: An animation module's closed export vocabulary and its refusals, as the renderer (compileAnimationModule here) and cadgen's build check (cadgen/_internal/animation_source.py) both say them. renderModule.test.js imports and compiles each source; tests/python/packages/cadgen/test_animation_source.py reads the same cases without running them. A refusal is the error's whole message; null is no refusal.
name: arm.py::arm animation

cases.why: a module that exports its clips and nothing else
cases.source: export const clips = { demo: { duration: 2, update(t, m) {} } };

cases.why: a helper exported beside the clips
cases.source:
export function helper() { return 1; }
export const clips = { demo: { duration: 2, update(t, m) { helper(); } } };
cases.error: arm.py::arm animation: unknown export helper — the renderer understands: clips

cases.why: every unknown export, in the order a module namespace lists them (by UTF-16 code unit)
cases.error: arm.py::arm animation: unknown exports HP, Helper, _clamp, clamp, solveDrs — the renderer understands: clips
arm.py::arm animation: a default export is not an animation-module export — use named exports (clips)

cases.why: an unknown export is reported before a default one
cases.error: arm.py::arm animation: unknown export extra — the renderer understands: clips

cases.why: a second binding of the exported declaration
cases.error: arm.py::arm animation: unknown export helper — the renderer understands: clips

cases.why: a line break ends the exported declaration before a statement it cannot continue into
a comma on the next line continues it
cases.error: arm.py::arm animation: unknown export helper — the renderer understands: clips

cases.why: the word export in comments, strings, templates, regular expressions and property names exports nothing
a quote inside a regular expression does not open a string
cases.error: arm.py::arm animation: unknown export helper — the renderer understands: clips
